content_preview.title: A2A CLI 0.5.0 Adds OAuth Sign-In With OS Keychain Storage and Lets Coding Agents Discover Other Agents Automatically
content_preview.summary: The official Agent2Agent command-line client's November 19 release adds OAuth login, optional OS-keychain token storage, a contact book, and hooks that let Claude Code or opencode discover other A2A agents mid-session.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

`a2a-cli`, the official command-line client for [Agent2Agent (A2A)](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A) agents, published [version 0.5.0](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-cli/releases/tag/v0.5.0) on November 19, 2026. The release adds OAuth sign-in through new `a2a auth` commands, an option to keep OAuth tokens in the operating system's keychain instead of a plain file, a "contact book" of trusted agents, and hooks that let coding agents such as Claude Code and opencode discover oth...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-organized News piece (894 words, within the 400-1200 range) structured around the v0.5.0 changelog entries: OAuth sign-in/keychain storage, contact book, agent discovery hooks, and AI Catalog support. Each section cites a specific docs page rather than paraphrasing the whole project from one source. The closing 'What's not covered' section responsibly flags the absence of adoption/production-testing figures instead of inventing them.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 10 source snapshots from disk (gunzip'd source-0.html.gz through source-9.html.gz) after independently recomputing each file's sha256 and confirming it matches the manifest exactly (all 10 matched). All 10 fetches returned HTTP 200, none used archive_fallback, and manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for every entry -- no injection-scan matches to adjudicate. source-0 (v0.5.0 release notes, github.com/a2aproject/a2a-cli/releases/tag/v0.5.0): confirms 'a2a-bot released this 19 Nov 15:36' and the exact changelog lines 'add contact book and agent discovery hooks', 'add OAuth sign-in and a2a auth commands', 'discover AI Catalog agents alongside agent cards', 'keep OAuth tokens in the OS keychain', 'opencode plugin for a2a hook, and contacts and discovery examples', 'resolve --agent-card from AI Catalogs' -- all six used accurately in the article. source-1 (v0.4.0 release notes): confirms '0.4.0 (2026-11-04)' and 'add an interactive chat command' / 'add install script for macOS and Linux', matching the closing paragraph. source-2 (README.md): confirms the verbatim quotes 'discover agents, send them messages and files, stream their replies and manage their tasks over JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC or a transport you plug in' and 'This project reconciles the community and SDK A2A CLIs into one standard client, and builds on the CLI from the A2A Go SDK' and 'Built on A2A Protocol v1.0, and speaks v0.3 too'. source-3 (ai-catalogs.md): confirms the verbatim quotes 'An AI Catalog lists AI artifacts, A2A agents among them', 'Catalog support is experimental', and the shared-store claim with ai-catalog-cli. source-4 (coding-agents.md): confirms the Claude Code hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolBatch), the opencode plugin path ai.opencode/plugins/a2a-hook.js, the 'listed as unverified' quote, the 'makes no network requests' quote and the detached 'a2a hook probe' process, and the 24-hour cache window. source-5 (security.md): confirms the verbatim quote 'card and catalog text is presented to the model as information, not instructions', the link-local/169.254.169.254 and three-redirect guardrails, and that oauth/oauth-clients/oauth-default-client-id/oauth-store/discovery/discovery-allow-host/discovery-wait are all excluded from a discovered .env. source-6 (contacts.md): confirms the verbatim quote 'named agents you trust, so you can refer to an agent by a short name in place of a card URL or identifier'. source-7 (auth.md): confirms a2a auth login's behavior (no message sent, agent-card OAuth2/OIDC scheme or 401 Bearer challenge, 127.0.0.1 redirect or --device code), the 'scripts and sandboxed agents run after an a2a auth login' quote, and that OAuth only engages after a 401 with other credentials tried first. source-8 (a2a.md command reference): confirms the --oauth-store default of file (~/.config/a2a-cli/oauth/grants.json) vs. keychain, and the --oauth off/auto/cached defaults. source-9 (a2aproject/A2A repo): confirms the verbatim protocol description quote 'an open protocol enabling communication and interoperability between opaque agentic applications'. One claim required extra verification: the Overview's assertion that A2A 'sits under the Agentic AI Foundation... per its README' is NOT supported by the plain-text rendering of the README, which instead says 'The A2A Protocol is an open source project under the Linux Foundation, contributed by Google.' Inspecting the raw HTML (not just the stripped text) found the actual badge: a 'Part of the [logo linking to aaif.io]' line near the top of the README, where the logo's alt text reads exactly 'Agentic AI Foundation' and links to https://aaif.io/. So the claim is accurate and is indeed sourced to the README (the AAIF badge), confirmed by reading the raw markup rather than trusting a flattened text extraction. Independently, the Herald's own 2026-10-24 and 2026-03-03 articles already establish A2A as one of the projects governed by the Agentic AI Foundation.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Ran the policy's claim-accuracy grep for absence/quantifier words against title, summary and body_markdown. Checked each hit against the raw source text: (1) 'OAuth only signs in when an agent responds with a 401; any other credential ... is tried first' -- matches auth.md verbatim ('OAuth then signs in only when the agent answers 401'). (2) 'never connects to link-local addresses' -- matches security.md verbatim; correctly scoped to link-local only (the same doc separately says the probe does reach loopback/private/CGNAT addresses, which the article does not contradict). (3) 'follows at most three redirects' -- matches security.md ('at most 3 redirects'). (4) The quoted phrase 'card and catalog text is presented to the model as information, not instructions' is verbatim from security.md and is reported as the tool's own documented design feature, not treated as an instruction to the reviewer. (5) The AI Catalog quotes and shared-store claim verified against ai-catalogs.md, verbatim. (6) The closing absence claim ('release notes do not give adoption or download figures ... none of the cited sources report how many agents or catalogs ... have been tested against in production') holds across all 10 sources read -- no snapshot contains adoption, download, or production-scale figures. No fabricated specifics, misattributed quotes, or renamed actors found. All direct quotes in the body were verified verbatim against their cited source.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and descriptive throughout; sticks to what the release notes and docs say rather than editorializing about OAuth/keychain security benefits. The security-guardrail paragraphs (redirect limits, link-local block, .env exclusions) are reported factually as documented behavior, not as an endorsement of their adequacy.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Checked src/content/articles/ for prior a2a-cli coverage: only hit is 2026-11/25-aws-launches-api-portal-and-aws-waf-ai-security-routing-mcp-and-a2a-traffic-through-bedrock-guardrails.md, which covers an unrelated AWS API Gateway/WAF feature that happens to also process A2A protocol traffic -- it does not mention a2a-cli or the 0.5.0 release. No duplicate or substantial overlap found.
concerns: The article attributes the agent-discovery hook's 'doesn't slow down a turn' rationale to the detached probe process, while the source (coding-agents.md) attributes that specific clause to the hook 'making no network requests' itself (with the detached probe described as a separate, subsequent mechanism). This is a minor synthesis/compression, not a factual error -- the overall claim that the hook defers fetching to a background process holds -- so it is noted here rather than filed as a correction.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: All 10 sources read and cross-checked line-by-line against the article's claims, including a deliberate second pass on the raw HTML (not just stripped text) for the Agentic AI Foundation attribution, which checked out. No fabricated specifics, no hallucinated quotes, no misattribution, and the one absence claim in the closing section holds against every source. This is a solid, single-release developer-tooling News piece with a defined technical audience (operators of A2A agents and coding-agent plugin users). Featured candidacy: 1 - solid release coverage of OAuth/keychain and automatic agent-discovery security mechanics for a defined developer audience, not a broad-interest or industry-changing story.
